learn: Review: present (hablo), preterite (hablé), imperfect (hablaba), future (hablaré), conditional (hablaría).
Preterite marks completed actions; imperfect describes background and habits.
Use context to choose the right tense.
lessons.try: Write a paragraph about your childhood using preterite and imperfect.

learn: Vocabulary: las raíces (roots), la herencia (heritage), las costumbres (customs), el idioma (language).
Many Spanish speakers in the US are bilingual and bicultural.
Identity can combine many cultures.
lessons.try: Write a short essay "¿Quién soy yo?" in Spanish.

learn: Traditions include el Día de los Muertos, las Posadas and la quinceañera.
Traditions vary by country and region.
Describe traditions with "se celebra" (it is celebrated).
check: A quinceañera celebrates a girl turning...
lessons.try: Present a Hispanic tradition and compare it with one of your own.

units.t: El subjuntivo con emociones y dudas

learn: Take the yo form, drop -o, add opposite endings: hablar becomes hable; comer becomes coma.
Irregulars: ser (sea), ir (vaya), saber (sepa), estar (esté), dar (dé), haber (haya).
The subjunctive appears in the second clause after "que".
lessons.try: Conjugate ten verbs in the present subjunctive.

learn: Use the subjunctive after emotions: Me alegro de que vengas.
Common triggers: alegrarse, sentir, temer, sorprender, esperar.
Same subject? Use the infinitive: Me alegro de estar aquí.
lessons.try: Write five sentences about how news makes you feel.

learn: Use the subjunctive after doubt: Dudo que llueva. No creo que sea verdad.
Certainty uses the indicative: Creo que es verdad.
Impersonal expressions: Es posible que, Es importante que.
lessons.try: Write opinions with "creo que" and "no creo que".

learn: Take the ellos preterite, drop -ron, add -ra endings: hablaron becomes hablara.
Irregulars follow the preterite: tuvieron becomes tuviera; fueron becomes fuera.
Nosotros forms take an accent: habláramos.
check: The imperfect subjunctive of tener (yo) is...
The imperfect subjunctive of ser (ellos) is...
The nosotros form of hablar is...
lessons.try: Conjugate ten verbs in the imperfect subjunctive.

learn: When the main verb is in the past, use the imperfect subjunctive: Quería que vinieras.
Triggers are the same as the present subjunctive.
Sequence of tenses keeps time consistent.
check: Past main verbs take the ___ subjunctive.
lessons.try: Rewrite present-subjunctive sentences in the past.

learn: Quisiera (I would like) is a polite form.
"Ojalá + imperfect subjunctive" expresses unlikely wishes: Ojalá tuviera más tiempo.
"Como si" (as if) always takes the imperfect subjunctive.
lessons.try: Write five wishes with "ojalá".

learn: Si + present, future/present: Si llueve, me quedo en casa.
These describe likely situations.
Commands are also possible: Si tienes tiempo, llámame.
lessons.try: Write five likely conditions about your week.

learn: Si + imperfect subjunctive, conditional: Si tuviera dinero, viajaría.
These describe unlikely or contrary-to-fact situations.
The order of clauses can switch.
lessons.try: Write "Si yo fuera presidente..." sentences.

learn: Si + pluperfect subjunctive, conditional perfect: Si hubiera estudiado, habría aprobado.
These express regrets about the past.
Hubiera = had (subjunctive); habría = would have.
lessons.try: Write about three things you would have done differently.

units.t: Los pronombres relativos y la literatura

learn: Que (that/which/who), quien (who, after prepositions), el que/la cual (which).
Lo que means "what" (the thing that): Lo que necesito es tiempo.
Cuyo agrees with the thing possessed: el autor cuyos libros leí.
lessons.try: Combine pairs of sentences using relative pronouns.

learn: El narrador, el personaje, el tema, la trama, el ambiente, la metáfora.
Spanish literature includes "Don Quijote" (1605) by Cervantes.
Latin American "realismo mágico" blends everyday life with magic.
check: Realismo mágico blends everyday life with...
lessons.try: Define five literary terms in Spanish with examples.

learn: José Martí's "Versos sencillos" (1891) became the song "Guantanamera".
Gustavo Adolfo Bécquer's "Rimas" are short Romantic poems.
Analyse rhyme, rhythm and imagery in Spanish.
lessons.try: Read and analyse a verse from "Versos sencillos".

learn: The Maya, Aztec (Mexica) and Inca built great civilisations.
Tenochtitlan was the Aztec capital; Cusco the Inca capital.
The Maya developed writing, mathematics with zero and calendars.
lessons.try: Present one civilisation in Spanish.

learn: Spanish conquest (1500s) brought colonisation, disease and forced labour.
Independence movements (1810-1825) were led by Simón Bolívar, José de San Martín and Miguel Hidalgo.
Mexico's "Grito de Dolores" (1810) began its war of independence.
lessons.try: Write a short biography of Bolívar in Spanish.

learn: The Mexican Revolution (1910-1920) changed land and power.
Many countries experienced dictatorships and returned to democracy.
Today Latin America has diverse economies and cultures.
lessons.try: Research a modern Latin American country and present it.

learn: El móvil/el celular, la red, las redes sociales, descargar, la contraseña, la aplicación.
Some English words are borrowed: el wifi, el email.
Discuss technology with "Uso... para...".
lessons.try: Describe how you use technology daily.

learn: Ventajas: comunicación, información, educación. Desventajas: adicción, privacidad, desinformación.
Express opinions: "En mi opinión...", "Por un lado... por otro lado...".
Use the subjunctive with "Es peligroso que...".
check: On the other side of the road
lessons.try: Debate whether phones should be allowed in class.

learn: Future tense: hablaré, comerás, vivirá; irregulars: tendré, haré, podré, diré.
Predict the future of technology.
Future of probability: ¿Dónde estará? (I wonder where it is.)
lessons.try: Write ten predictions for 2050.

units.t: El arte, la música y el cine

learn: Diego Velázquez painted "Las Meninas" (1656); Francisco Goya documented war and society.
Frida Kahlo and Diego Rivera shaped Mexican art; Rivera painted murals.
Describe art: "En el cuadro se ve...", "Los colores son...".
lessons.try: Describe a famous painting in Spanish.

learn: Genres: salsa, merengue, cumbia, tango, flamenco, reggaetón, mariachi.
Music blends Indigenous, African and European roots.
Describe music: el ritmo, la letra, la melodía.
check: "La letra" of a song means the...
Salsa developed among Caribbean communities in...
lessons.try: Present a Spanish-language music genre.

learn: Film vocabulary: la película, el director, los actores, el guion, los subtítulos.
Write a film review: la trama, la actuación, la recomendación.
Spain, Mexico and Argentina have strong film industries.
lessons.try: Write a review of a Spanish-language film.

learn: Vocabulary: la contaminación, el cambio climático, reciclar, la deforestación, la energía renovable.
The Amazon rainforest spans several South American countries.
Propose solutions with "Deberíamos..." (we should).
lessons.try: Write a proposal to protect the environment.

learn: La pobreza, la desigualdad, la inmigración, los derechos humanos.
Discuss causes and effects: "porque", "por lo tanto", "como resultado".
Respect multiple perspectives.
lessons.try: Debate a social issue in Spanish.

learn: Volunteer vocabulary: el voluntariado, la ONG, ayudar, donar, la comunidad.
Use the subjunctive: "Es necesario que ayudemos".
Small local actions add up.
lessons.try: Plan a community service project in Spanish.

units.t: El discurso indirecto y la presentación final

learn: Direct: Ana dice: "Tengo hambre." Indirect: Ana dice que tiene hambre.
Past reporting shifts tenses: Ana dijo que tenía hambre.
Pronouns and time words change: hoy becomes ese día.
lessons.try: Convert ten direct quotes to reported speech.

learn: Reported commands use the subjunctive: "Me pidió que cerrara la puerta."
Present reporting: "Me dice que estudie."
Verbs: pedir, decir, mandar, sugerir.
lessons.try: Report five instructions your teacher gave you.

learn: Choose a topic connecting Hispanic culture to your interests.
Use varied tenses, the subjunctive and connectors.
Speak for five minutes with visuals and answer questions.
lessons.try: Give a five-minute presentation in Spanish.
